# Legal Memorandum: Application of WARN Act Thresholds to Reductions in Force
Client Advisory Note

## Client and Facility Details
| Facility Location | Active Full-Time Employees | Active Part-Time Employees | Planned Terminations (Effective 05/15/2026) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Site A (Dallas Facility) | 180 | 25 | 60 |
| Site B (Plano Facility) | 45 | 10 | 22 |

## Statutory Framework
Under 29 U.S.C. Section 2101 et seq., the federal WARN Act applies to business enterprises employing at least 100 full-time employees, or 100 or more employees who in the aggregate work at least 4,000 hours per week. Advance notice must be provided at least 60 calendar days prior to a qualifying employment loss.

A mass layoff triggers notice requirements if an employment loss affects at least 33 percent of active full-time workers and at least 50 full-time workers at a single site of employment. Alternatively, an employment loss of 500 or more full-time employees triggers notice regardless of the percentage of the workforce affected.

## Analysis
- Site A currently maintains 180 active full-time personnel, meaning the planned termination of 60 full-time workers represents exactly 30 percent of the site's full-time workforce.
- Because 60 terminations exceeds the absolute threshold of 50 full-time workers and satisfies the 33 percent requirement, Site A qualifies as a covered mass layoff.
- Site B does not trigger mass layoff provisions on a standalone basis because total terminations remain well below the minimum threshold of 50 affected full-time workers.
- The Dallas and Plano facilities operate under distinct operational management and geographic separation, precluding single-site aggregation under 20 CFR Section 639.3(i).

## Recommended Actions
- Issue formal written notice to Dallas site employees and the Texas Workforce Commission on or before 03/16/2026.
- Maintain standard non-WARN separation workflows for all departing Plano facility personnel.
